conventions: Package name remains glowflow; public API uses exported Go structs and interfaces.
Definition structs in define.go carry JSON tags and are consumed by compiler/engine.
Runtime flow terms are pervasive and should stay unless tied to exported definition object names.
Tests are package-local Go tests using direct struct literals.

hard: Do not implement during planning phase.
Use apply_patch for later implementation edits.
Do not revert unrelated user changes.
Do not rename runtime symbols unless directly required by definition object type references.
soft: Prefer compilation/search validation over broad refactors.
compatibility: FlowMetadata and FlowDefinition are exported; rename is a breaking API change.
JSON field names should remain stable unless explicit requirements change.

patterns: compiler.go compiles definition inputs into CompiledFlow runtime topology.
engine.go stores definitions and compiled runtime by flow ID/version.
tests instantiate definition structs directly to exercise compiler and engine behavior.

responsibility: Store compiled runtime per flow ID/version.

purpose: Primary owner of FlowMetadata and FlowDefinition.

prior_decisions.decision: Rename only exported definition object types FlowMetadata and FlowDefinition.
rationale: User asked for Flow* objects in define.go because package name already ends with flow.
Other Flow names represent compiler/runtime flow concepts, not definition objects.
Request concerns Go object names, not serialized schema.
Changing JSON would expand compatibility risk without explicit requirement.
